name: Ocean Source-Adapter Runners (GitHub + Telegram First)
purpose: Replace facade source adapters with real server-side fetch/ingest runners, starting with GitHub and Telegram per docs/SOURCE-ADAPTER-PRECEDENTS.md. Each runner fetches remote content, dedupes by content hash, writes objects through the storage router (built in ocean-longhouse-router), records the existing source_instance -> source_stream -> source_sync_run -> source_record lineage plus Ocean Ledger events, persists incremental cursors in longhouse.ledger_source_cursors, and only advertises capabilities (delete_detection/webhook/incremental) that are actually implemented. Stops longhouse.source_adapters from advertising GitHub/Telegram/Slack/Notion/Linear/Drive/R2 capabilities that have no runner behind them.

canonicalBoundaries.oceanDaemon: Local runtime/body and execution authority. Owns local sessions, events, tools, provider execution, local filesystem/shell/destructive permissions.
canonicalBoundaries.oceanLonghouse: Hive brain / coordination layer per ocean-os/docs/LONGHOUSE.md. Coordinates skills, SOPs, routines, MCP discovery, memory, subagents, quorum/council logic. Does not bypass daemon permissions.
canonicalBoundaries.oceanBedrock: Cloud-box support substrate for shared files, context ingest, ledger/event store, Postgres/R2/Vectorize/KV, MCP-facing infrastructure, and coworker bootstrap. Does not redefine Longhouse.

currentState: Today only local_folder has a working runner, and even that runs client-side: scripts/ocean-ingest-local.mjs walks the disk and PUTs files, while the server only exposes three thin HTTP coordination handlers (handleLocalFolderPlan ~server.mjs:948, handleLocalFolderRecordsBatch ~1020, handleLocalFolderCommit ~1067) that wrap src/sources.mjs helpers (upsertSourceInstance/upsertSourceStream/createSourceSyncRun/upsertSourceRecord/completeSourceSyncRun). The other 7 adapters are registry rows only: db/003_source_adapters.sql and the DEFAULT_ADAPTERS array in src/sources.mjs (lines 80-315) seed github/telegram/etc with capabilities JSON claiming incremental/webhook/delete_detection that no code delivers. There is NO server-side SourceRunner abstraction, NO remote fetch (no GitHub/Telegram HTTP client anywhere), and NO secret resolver: secret_ref is stored on source_instances (sources.mjs:730, server.mjs:730) but never read by anything. Incremental cursors have two unconnected homes: source_streams.cursor (jsonb, written by local-folder plan) and longhouse.ledger_source_cursors (db/002:91-101, a proper per-source cursor table) which is currently UNUSED by any adapter. Object writes go through putFile/recordObjectWrite against a single hardcoded local disk root (state.filesRoot), which the ocean-longhouse-router wave replaces with a storage router this wave depends on.

phases.title: Pin boundaries, runner contract, and honest capabilities
tasks: Reaffirm canonical boundary: source runners are ocean-bedrock substrate code that fetch remote bytes/events and record lineage; they do NOT redefine Longhouse coordination or claim Bedrock is the quorum engine.

Read src/sources.mjs (DEFAULT_ADAPTERS lines 80-315), db/003_source_adapters.sql, db/002_ocean_ledger.sql (ledger_source_cursors), docs/SOURCE-ADAPTER-PRECEDENTS.md, scripts/ocean-ingest-local.mjs, and the local-folder handlers in src/server.mjs (948-1081) before writing any runner.

Establish the rule that capabilities JSON (snapshot/incremental/webhook/delete_detection) is a CONTRACT: a flag may only be true when a runner implements it. Audit current github (delete_detection:true in db/003 vs false in sources.mjs DEFAULT_ADAPTERS) and telegram (snapshot:false) for the existing drift and record the target honest values.

Decide and document the precedence between source_streams.cursor and longhouse.ledger_source_cursors: this track uses ledger_source_cursors as the authoritative incremental checkpoint store keyed by source_id='<adapter>:<instance>:<stream>', and treats source_streams.cursor as a denormalized convenience mirror only.

Define the SourceRunner interface contract on paper (plan() -> fetch()/iterate() -> writeObject() -> recordRecord() -> commit()) paralleling the local_folder plan -> records:batch -> commit HTTP flow, but executed server-side since remote adapters have no local courier.
acceptance: A short RUNNER-CONTRACT note in docs states runners must keep capabilities honest and never write raw secrets to source_instances.config or manifests.
Capability-drift table lists current vs target capabilities for local_folder/github/telegram with the db/003-vs-sources.mjs github delete_detection mismatch explicitly called out.
Decision recorded: ledger_source_cursors is authoritative cursor store; source_streams.cursor is a mirror.
Note explicitly defers slack/notion/linear/google_drive/r2 runners to a later wave and states their capabilities must be downgraded to facade-honest values until implemented.

phases.title: Build the server-side SourceRunner interface and registry
tasks: Create src/sources/runner.mjs defining a SourceRunner base contract: async plan(ctx), async *iterate(ctx) yielding normalized document packets ({source_record_id, virtual_path, content, content_type, content_sha256, source_updated_at, metadata}) matching the docs/SOURCE-ADAPTER-PRECEDENTS.md packet shape, and a default commit(ctx, stats).

Create src/sources/registry.mjs mapping adapter_id -> runner factory, registering only adapters with real runners; getRunner(adapterId) throws a clear 'no runner implemented for <adapter>' error for facade adapters so the server cannot pretend to sync them.

Implement a shared orchestration helper runSourceSync(db, state, {instance, stream, mode}) in src/sources/runner.mjs that: calls createSourceSyncRun, loads the cursor from ledger_source_cursors, drives the runner's iterate(), writes each packet's bytes through the storage router (from ocean-longhouse-router) under the stream's remote_prefix, dedupes via content_sha256 against existing source_records, calls upsertSourceRecord for lineage, advances the cursor, and calls completeSourceSyncRun/failSourceSyncRun.

Add a content-hash dedupe guard: before writing an object, look up source_records by (source_instance_id, source_record_id); skip the object write when content_sha256 is unchanged (increment skipped_count), matching the local courier's prior.sha256 check in scripts/ocean-ingest-local.mjs.
Reuse src/sources.mjs helpers unchanged for all lineage/ledger emission; do not duplicate ledger logic in runners.
acceptance: src/sources/runner.mjs exports SourceRunner, runSourceSync; src/sources/registry.mjs exports getRunner/listRunnerAdapters.
getRunner('slack') throws 'no runner implemented'; getRunner('github') and getRunner('telegram') return runner instances.

A unit/integration test drives runSourceSync with a fake runner yielding 2 packets and asserts source_sync_runs gets one completed row, 2 source_records rows, and matching ledger events (source.sync.started/source.record.ingested/source.sync.completed).
Re-running the same fake runner with identical content yields skipped_count=2 and uploaded_count=0 (dedupe verified).

phases.title: Secret-ref resolver and ledger_source_cursors integration
tasks: Create src/sources/secrets.mjs implementing resolveSecret(secret_ref) that maps a secret_ref string (e.g. 'env:GITHUB_TOKEN', 'env:TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN') to process.env, returning the raw token only in-memory; NEVER persist resolved tokens to Postgres, manifests, or ledger payloads.

Define the secret_ref convention: source_instances.secret_ref holds a pointer like 'env:VAR_NAME' (and a documented future 'kv:<key>' form), validated against an allowlist regex; reject any secret_ref that looks like a raw token (length/charset heuristic) at instance-create time in src/server.mjs sourceInstancePayload (~line 719).

Create src/sources/cursors.mjs with getCursor(db, sourceId)/setCursor(db, sourceId, {cursor_value, source_type, last_event_timestamp, status, error, metadata}) wrapping longhouse.ledger_source_cursors (db/002:91-101) via upsert on source_id PRIMARY KEY.

Wire runSourceSync to read the incremental cursor before fetch and persist the advanced cursor after a successful commit; on failure, set ledger_source_cursors.status='failed' and error without advancing cursor_value.

Add redaction: ensure ledger payloads, source_records.metadata, and sync-run metadata never include Authorization headers, tokens, or full webhook secrets (store only a sha256 fingerprint of the webhook secret if needed).
acceptance: resolveSecret('env:GITHUB_TOKEN') returns the env value; resolveSecret of a missing var throws a clear error naming the missing env var, not the value.
Creating a source_instance with secret_ref that matches a raw-token heuristic returns HTTP 400 and is rejected.
After a sync run, SELECT cursor_value FROM longhouse.ledger_source_cursors WHERE source_id='github:<inst>:<stream>' returns the advanced commit SHA / update_id.
grep over ledger_events.payload and source_records.metadata for a known test token value returns zero rows.

phases.title: Implement the GitHub repository-contents runner (poll + incremental)
tasks: Create src/sources/github.mjs implementing a SourceRunner for adapter_id 'github', stream_type 'contents': use the GitHub REST API (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{branch}?recursive=1 for snapshot; GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits and compare API for incremental) authenticated with the token from resolveSecret(instance.secret_ref).

Map config {owner, repo, branch, paths} (config_schema in db/003:121) to fetched blobs; for each file blob, fetch raw content, compute content_sha256, and map to virtual_path under the stream remote_prefix (default '/context/github/<owner>/<repo>/<path>' or '/coworkers/...' when owner-scoped), yielding normalized packets.

Implement incremental sync using the last synced commit SHA stored in ledger_source_cursors: on incremental runs call the compare API (base=lastSha, head=branch) and only re-fetch changed/added files; advance cursor to the new head SHA on commit.

Respect GitHub rate limits: read X-RateLimit-Remaining/Reset headers, back off (sleep until reset) when remaining is low, set a conservative per-run file cap, and record rate-limit state in sync-run metadata (not secrets).

Honor capabilities: implement delete_detection via the compare API 'removed' file status (soft-delete by setting source_records.deleted_at), so github delete_detection can be truthfully set true; leave webhook false until phase-5.

Add a server route POST /api/v1/sources/instances/:id/sync (admin/write + path-scope checked) that resolves the instance's adapter, calls getRunner + runSourceSync, and returns the sync-run summary; register it in the router near the existing /api/v1/sync/local-folder/* block (src/server.mjs ~1615).
acceptance: POST /api/v1/sources/instances/<github-id>/sync against a real small public test repo writes files under the stream remote_prefix and creates source_records with content_sha256 + object_id.
A second sync with no upstream changes returns skipped_count>0, uploaded_count=0, and does not move the cursor backward.
After pushing one commit upstream, an incremental sync uploads only the changed file(s) and advances ledger_source_cursors.cursor_value to the new head SHA.
Deleting a file upstream then syncing sets source_records.deleted_at for that record (delete_detection proven before the capability flag is flipped).

phases.title: Implement the Telegram chat runner (incremental getUpdates)
tasks: Create src/sources/telegram.mjs implementing a SourceRunner for adapter_id 'telegram': use the Bot API getUpdates with offset=<last update_id + 1> stored in ledger_source_cursors (matching the precedent 'telegram: chat_id + update_id/message_id' in docs/SOURCE-ADAPTER-PRECEDENTS.md), authenticated with resolveSecret(instance.secret_ref) (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN).

Filter updates to the configured config.chat_id (db/003:129); for each message render a normalized markdown packet (text + author + timestamp + external metadata) at virtual_path like '/context/telegram/<chat>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<message_id>.md', compute content_sha256, and yield it.

For media messages, record media metadata (file_id, mime, size) in source_records.metadata; optionally fetch media bytes via getFile + file download when within size limits and binary_files capability is honored; otherwise skip bytes and keep the metadata record.
Advance the cursor to max(update_id)+1 on commit; getUpdates is inherently incremental-only, so keep snapshot:false honest and do NOT claim a snapshot capability.
Respect Telegram rate limits and long-poll timeout bounds; cap updates fetched per run; record next offset and counts in sync-run metadata.
Route the same POST /api/v1/sources/instances/:id/sync added in phase-3 through the telegram runner via the registry (no new route needed).
acceptance: With a test bot + chat, POST /api/v1/sources/instances/<telegram-id>/sync ingests recent messages as objects under the chat remote_prefix with source_records + ledger events.
A second immediate sync returns 0 new records (offset cursor consumed) and the cursor_value equals the last update_id+1.
Sending a new message then syncing ingests exactly that message (incremental proven).
telegram capabilities in the registry keep snapshot:false; no code path claims a full-history snapshot.

phases.title: Webhook receivers and capability reconciliation
tasks: Add a webhook receiver route POST /api/v1/sources/webhooks/:adapter/:instanceId in src/server.mjs that verifies the signature (GitHub X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC using a per-instance webhook secret resolved via secret_ref; Telegram secret_token header) before processing.

On a verified GitHub push webhook, enqueue/trigger an incremental sync for the affected branch (reuse runSourceSync); on a verified Telegram update webhook, ingest the single update and advance the cursor. Reject unverified payloads with 401 and emit a ledger security event.

Update src/sources.mjs DEFAULT_ADAPTERS and write a new db/004_source_capabilities_truth.sql migration that flips capabilities to reflect ONLY what is implemented: github {snapshot:true, incremental:true, webhook:true(after this phase), delete_detection:true, ...}; telegram {snapshot:false, incremental:true, webhook:true(after this phase), delete_detection:false}; and DOWNGRADE slack/notion/linear/google_drive/r2 webhook/incremental/delete_detection flags to false until runners exist, resolving the db/003-vs-sources.mjs drift found in phase-0.

Make getRunner the single source of truth: add a /api/v1/sources/adapters response field 'runner_implemented' derived from listRunnerAdapters so the registry API never advertises a capability the runner cannot deliver.
Document env var requirements (GITHUB_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, per-instance webhook secrets) and the Railway variable names in docs, without putting any secret value in the repo.
acceptance: A forged GitHub webhook (bad signature) is rejected 401 and logged as a ledger security event; a correctly-signed push triggers an incremental sync.
GET /api/v1/sources/adapters shows runner_implemented:true only for local_folder/github/telegram and false for the other 5.
db/004 applied to prod: capabilities.webhook/delete_detection are true ONLY for adapters with implemented behavior; slack/notion/linear/google_drive/r2 incremental+webhook+delete_detection are false.
No remaining capability flag is true without a corresponding code path (verified by cross-checking registry against listRunnerAdapters).

phases.title: Security and launch review for source runners
tasks: Audit that no raw GitHub/Telegram token or webhook secret appears in source_instances.config, source_records.metadata, ledger_events.payload, sync-run metadata, manifests, or logs; only secret_ref pointers and sha256 fingerprints are persisted.

Confirm the new /api/v1/sources/instances/:id/sync and /api/v1/sources/webhooks/* routes enforce requirePermission + requirePathScope + requireClearance consistent with existing source handlers (src/server.mjs handleSourceInstances ~763), and that webhook routes verify signatures before any DB write.
Verify delete_detection only soft-deletes (sets deleted_at) and never performs destructive remote mirroring, per docs/SOURCE-ADAPTER-PRECEDENTS.md guidance #8.
Confirm rate-limit backoff prevents runaway API usage and that a single bad instance cannot stall the whole service (per-run caps, failure isolation, ledger_source_cursors.status='failed').
Produce an operator runbook: how to register a github/telegram instance with secret_ref, set the env var on Railway, trigger a manual sync, register a webhook, and rotate/revoke a secret.
acceptance: Security checklist passes: zero raw secrets in any persisted artifact (grep-verified for test tokens).
Both new route families reject unauthorized/unscoped/unsigned requests in tests.
Capabilities are demonstrably honest: every true flag has a passing acceptance test from phases 3-5 behind it.
Operator runbook exists and known gaps (slack/notion/linear/drive/r2 still facade) are documented as future, not implied complete.

launchDefinitionOfDone: A server-side SourceRunner interface (src/sources/runner.mjs) drives plan -> iterate -> writeObject -> recordRecord -> commit, reusing src/sources.mjs lineage helpers and the ocean-longhouse-router storage router.

GitHub runner performs a real snapshot + incremental sync of a test repo: objects written, source_records with content_sha256+object_id created, cursor advanced in ledger_source_cursors, delete_detection soft-deletes via deleted_at.
Telegram runner performs a real incremental getUpdates sync of a test chat: messages ingested as objects, offset cursor advanced to update_id+1, second sync yields zero new records.

Credentials are resolved from env via secret_ref (src/sources/secrets.mjs); zero raw tokens or webhook secrets exist in source_instances.config, source_records.metadata, ledger payloads, manifests, or logs.
Incremental cursors are stored in longhouse.ledger_source_cursors and survive across runs; re-sync of unchanged content yields skipped_count>0 and uploaded_count=0 (dedupe by content hash proven).
Verified webhook receivers exist for GitHub (HMAC) and Telegram (secret_token); forged payloads are rejected 401 and logged.

longhouse.source_adapters.capabilities is honest: every true flag (incremental/webhook/delete_detection) maps to an implemented runner behavior; slack/notion/linear/google_drive/r2 unimplemented flags are downgraded to false via db/004, and GET /api/v1/sources/adapters exposes runner_implemented.

Security review confirms scoped/clearance-checked sync routes, non-destructive delete, rate-limit backoff, and no secret leakage; operator runbook (docs/SOURCE-RUNNERS.md) documents registration, env vars, webhooks, and rotation.
openDecisions: Sync execution model: synchronous within the HTTP request (simplest, like local-folder commit) vs enqueued into the existing-but-unused worker loop (server.mjs ~line 1187) / longhouse.ingest_jobs. Recommend synchronous-with-per-run-cap for v1, queue later for large repos.

Whether per-instance webhook secrets live as their own secret_ref env vars or a hashed value column; the schema currently has only one secret_ref per instance, which may be insufficient for instances that need both an API token AND a webhook secret.

Virtual-path placement policy: remote source content under /context/<adapter>/... (shared knowledge) vs /coworkers/<name>/... (owner-scoped). Needs a convention decision aligned with the path-scope/clearance model before GitHub/Telegram go live.

This track is assigned firingOrder=3 depending on ocean-longhouse-router (wave 2) for the storage router that writeObject targets. If the router slips, runners could fall back to the current putFile/recordObjectWrite local-disk path as an interim, but that re-couples to state.filesRoot and should be avoided — flagged as a risk.

Telegram getUpdates and webhook are mutually exclusive in the Bot API (a bot cannot use getUpdates while a webhook is set). The spec must pick poll OR webhook per telegram instance, not both simultaneously.
Whether to backfill/retry the 9 historical failed longhouse.ingest_jobs as part of this track or leave to a cleanup track (likely out of scope here).
risks: Hard dependency on ocean-longhouse-router (wave 2): runners write objects through the storage router. If that router is not ready, writeObject has no honest target except the hardcoded local disk root (state.filesRoot / recordObjectWrite mount_id='managed-local'), which re-introduces the single-mount coupling this track is meant to avoid. This is the primary cross-wave risk — the assigned dependsOnWorkflows=['ocean-longhouse-router'] is correct, do not start runner object-writes before the router lands.

Capability dishonesty is currently shipping to prod: db/003 and src/sources.mjs DEFAULT_ADAPTERS already disagree (github delete_detection true in db/003 vs false in sources.mjs) and both advertise webhook/incremental for adapters with no runner. Until db/004 lands, the registry actively lies to agents/coworkers about what it can sync.

Secret handling: secret_ref is stored but never consumed today, so there is no precedent resolver. A sloppy implementation could log tokens or write them into source_records.metadata/ledger payloads; phase-2 and phase-6 must gate this hard.

GitHub rate limits (5000 req/hr authenticated, lower for trees on large repos) can stall syncs or exhaust quota; without per-run caps and backoff a single large repo instance could degrade the whole single-replica service.

Telegram getUpdates offset is consume-once: a bug that advances the cursor before objects are durably written would silently drop messages. Cursor advance MUST happen only after a successful commit, with failure leaving cursor_value unmoved and status='failed'.

Token registry and tokens are single-replica file-based (data/.ocean-bedrock/tokens.json); webhook receivers may be hit by external traffic and must not assume the same auth model as scoped coworker tokens — signature verification, not bearer tokens, secures webhook routes.
Mapping remote items to virtual paths can collide with existing /context or /coworkers content; without a clear namespacing convention (open decision) a runner could overwrite human-authored objects.
